intended_object: The isomorphism class [M] of a finitely generated projective right R-module M, viewed as an element of the commutative monoid (under ⊕) of such classes. This is the monoid whose group completion is K₀(R). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`ProjectiveClass R` is the skeleton of the category of finitely generated projective Rᵐᵒᵖ-modules (that is, right R-modules), shrunk to universe u. Its monoid structure comes from the chosen-product (direct-sum) Cartesian monoidal structure. `of R M` takes the representative of M in universe u (`repr`), sends it to the skeleton with `toSkeleton`, and transports the result along the Shrink equivalence. So it is exactly the isomorphism class of M.

The lemmas that follow confirm this:
- `of_eq_iff`: two classes are equal iff the modules are linearly isomorphic.
- `of_prod`: the class of M × N is the sum of the classes.
- `of_zero`: the zero module has class 0.

R is an arbitrary ring and M can live in any universe, so this is the natural generality. Using right modules as `Module Rᵐᵒᵖ` follows Weibel's convention and is a legitimate choice. Mathlib has no monoid of isomorphism classes of projective modules and no K₀ of a ring, so there is no general counterpart to cite.
